voiceover: Someone calls your phone carrier, pretends to be you, and moves your number to their SIM card. That's a SIM swap. Now every text code goes to them, including the one that resets your email. Two factor login still matters, and any version beats none. But a text message is the weakest kind, because phone numbers can be taken over. An authenticator app keeps your codes on your own device. Passkeys and security keys are stronger still, because they only work on the real site, so a fake login page gets nothing. Switch your email account first. Send this to whoever still uses text codes.
